We have mass spec showing m/z 182.073... likely molecular ion (M+). So molecular weight ~182.07. Proton NMR shows a single signal at 7.51 ppm, dddd, J couplings, integrating to 10H. That's aromatic protons (10 H). So likely a symmetric aromatic compound with 10 aromatic protons, maybe biphenyl? But biphenyl has 10 aromatic H and MW 154.21. Not 182. So maybe a phenyl group attached to something else but still 10 aromatic H suggests two phenyl rings? Actually each phenyl has 5 H. Two phenyls give 10 H. So compound likely C12H10? That's 154.2. Not 182. So maybe there are additional atoms but aromatic protons still 10, meaning maybe a phenyl attached to a carbonyl etc that reduces H count? But aromatic protons count remains 10. Could be diphenyl ether (C12H10O) MW 170.2. Not 182. Could be diphenyl sulfone (C12H10O2S) MW 218. Not 182. Could be diphenylmethane (C13H12) MW 168.2. Not 182. Could be biphenyl with a substituent that adds mass but doesn't affect aromatic H count, e.g., biphenyl with a CH2 group attached to one ring replacing a H, but then aromatic H count would be 9. So need 10 aromatic H, meaning both rings are unsubstituted (no substituents). So maybe the molecule is a dimer of phenyl with something else that doesn't affect aromatic H count, like a carbonyl bridging? But that would replace a hydrogen on each ring? Actually if you have benzophenone (diphenyl ketone) C13H10O, aromatic H count is 10 (each phenyl has 5). MW = 182.22! Yes benzophenone (diphenyl ketone) formula C13H10O, MW 182.22. That matches mass spec 182.07 (close). So likely benzophenone.

Proton NMR of benzophenone: aromatic protons appear as multiplet around 7.5 ppm, integrating to 10 H. Yes.

Thus SMILES: O=C(c1ccccc1)c2ccccc2 . That's "O=C(c1ccccc1)c2ccccc2". Or "O=C(c1ccccc1)c2ccccc2". Provide final answer.

We could validate with get_formula_from_smiles.
